about: Fragment selection for the nfr workflow. Its required set in step-01 is unconditional, and one member of it (playwright-config.md) is named with no stack gate at all, so the backend case below asserts the step file as written rather than what the fragment name suggests.

cases.name: NFR assessment for a JVM service with no browser anywhere
cases.prompt: Assess the settlement service against our reliability and performance NFRs and tell me what evidence is missing.
repoFacts: Gradle project with JUnit 5 and Testcontainers; there is no package.json in the repo
no browser automation of any kind, no .maestro directory, no pact artifacts
docs/nfr.md states a 99.9% availability target and a p95 latency budget

assertions.text: The step file names all five as required with no stack condition, including playwright-config.md. Ground truth here is the step file as written, not what the fragment name implies; if that unconditional include is wrong it is a bug in the workflow, and this case is what would make it visible rather than something the eval should quietly correct.
Both library flags default true and neither package can be present in a Gradle repo with no JavaScript manifest, so both mandates stay closed. The flag alone is never sufficient.

cases.name: NFR assessment where browser automation is set to cli
cases.prompt: Assess the checkout experience against our performance and accessibility NFRs and list the evidence gaps.

assertions.text: playwright-cli.md is gated on tea_browser_automation being cli or auto, which is a config value rather than a property of the repository. This is the pair to the backend case, where the same key is none and the fragment must not load.
